fixes.explanation: Eliezer isn't in this passage, baker. Abraham's servant is a fair name to reach for, since this family has a lot of names floating around. Rebekah tells Jacob, "…flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran." (Gen 27:43) Laban is her brother, and that's who she names.

Noah's a big name, baker, but he's not in this blessing. Isaac says, "And may He give the blessing of Abraham to you and your descendants…" (Gen 28:4) The name in the verse is Abraham, and he's Isaac's own father (Gen 25:19). Isaac is handing down a blessing the way a dad hands down a recipe card, straight from his own family.

No branches here, baker. Jacob spent the night there "…because the sun had set," and he took "…one of the stones from that place…" (Gen 28:11) Picture it. A whole night out there, and his headrest is a rock. I've slept in a junk drawer on a pile of takeout menus, and even I think that sounds rough.

A tower is a fair guess, since it also goes up high. But the dream isn't about one. The text says it was "…a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven…" (Gen 28:12) A tower you walk around and admire. A ladder, baker? That's one you climb, and it's the one Jacob sees.

The dream shows "…God’s angels were going up and down the ladder." (Gen 28:12) Up AND down, baker. Nobody's stuck at the bottom waiting for a turn. Jacob is lying there on a stone with his head on the ground, and heaven is busy right above him.

Jacob says, "…of all that You give me I will surely give You a tenth." (Gen 28:22) One out of every ten. Say a batch comes out of my oven with ten cookies. One of them goes to God. Notice he says "all" that God gives him, so nothing is left out of the count.

A third is a lot bigger than what Jacob says, baker. A third of ten cookies is more than three, and he's only talking about one. Jacob says, "…of all that You give me I will surely give You a tenth." (Gen 28:22) The word in the verse is tenth, and he says it about all that God gives him.
